title.narrative: Water Supply and Sanitation Services Investment Program - Tranche 3

description.narrative: On 28 August 2009, the Government of the Republic of Uzbekistan (the Government) signed a Financing Framework Agreement (FFA) with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for a multitranche financing facility (MFF) to finance the Water Supply and Sanitation (WSS) Services Investment Program, in an aggregate amount not exceeding $300 million from ADB Special Funds resources. On 29 September 2009, the ADB Board of Directors approved the MFF WSS Investment Program with the Uzbekistan Communal Services Agency (UCSA) as the executing agency. The investment program combines physical and non-physical improvements in water supply and wastewater management sectors through investment and institutional strengthening and capacity building. The investment program's outcome is safer and more reliable WSS services and improved hygiene in targeted towns. On 30 September 2011, the Government submitted a periodic financing request (PFR3) to ADB for a loan of $59 million for the third tranche (Project 3). PFR 3 will finance (i) expansion and rehabilitation of water supply systems in Karakalpakstan, Khorezm, and Djizzak provinces; (ii) expansion and rehabilitation of wastewater networks in Andijan; and (iii) capacity development and project management support. Rehabilitation and expansion of WSS systems and development of vodokanals' O&M capacity are urgently needed to prevent the systems from further deterioration and provide improved WSS services to residents in 11 project regions.

Safe, reliable, and sustainable water supply, improved sanitation services and hygiene in project towns.

Electricity consumption reduced to 0.8 kwh/m3 (baseline 2010: 2.1 kwh/m3) Progress/Status: All WSS facilities are equipped with modern and less energy consuming technologies. Assessment will be made during PCR preparation. Data Source: Vodokanal records, financial reports, and performance benchmarking reports Actual value:

Safe, reliable water with national drinking water standard provided to 257,000 people at least 20 hours a day in Amudaryinsky, Beruniysky, Kegeyliysky, Hodjeyliysky, and Shumanaysky of Karakalpakstan, Koshkupirsky, Khivinsky and Yangiariksky of Khorezm, and Zafarabad and Arnasai of Djizzak by 2016 (baseline 2011: There is no water supply in eight project regions of Karakalpakstan and Khorezm; 26,700 people in the two project regions of Djizzak have piped water supply 1-2 hours a day. Water quality does not comply with the national standard) Progress/Status: All civil works contracts have been completed. WSS facilities have been fully commissioned and operationalized. Close to 300,000 people in project areas now have access to safe, reliable water supply. Data Source: Vodokanal records, financial reports, and performance benchmarking reports Actual value:

Collection rate of water supply tariff and sanitation charges in the eleven project regions increased to 90% by 2016 (baseline 2010: tariff collection rate 35%, Djizzak) Progress/Status: Collection rate of water supply tariff and sanitation charges is in the range of 85-100%. Data Source: Vodokanal records, financial reports, and performance benchmarking reports Actual value:

Additional 29,700 people, or 46.8% of the population of Andijan will have access to sewerage network and will have sewerage services. Quality of sewage service of 154,510 people in Andijan will be improved (baseline 2011: 38.9% of population covered by sewerage service, with leakage rate of 30% in Andijan) Progress/Status: Additional 30,155 now have sewerage services. Close to 170,000 people are now connected to sewerage network in Andijan city. More than 95% of civil works on rehabilitation of Andijan city sewerage network system has been completed. Remaining works are expected to be completed by the end of January 2018. Data Source: Vodokanal records, financial reports, and performance benchmarking reports Actual value:

Time spent by women and children to fetch water in the ten project regions of Karakalpakstan, Khorezm and Djizzak reduced to less than 1 day/month in project regions (baseline 2010: 4 days per month in the 10 project regions) Progress/Status: During interviews with project beneficiaries, it has been confirmed that the time spent to fetch water by women and children have significantly reduced to 2-3 hours/day. Data Source: Vodokanal records, financial reports, and performance benchmarking reports Actual value:

Assessment will be made during PCR preparation. Data Source: Vodokanal records, financial reports, and performance benchmarking reports Actual value:
